raw_response:
I will not start from zero. I will do mostly what worked for me last year, then adjust a little by crop. On 12 mu, I cannot gamble too much. Wheat and maize are still my base because that is the steady part of the money, and with my well I do not fear drought as much as dryland people do. For cabbage, cauliflower, chili, and eggplant, I will keep smaller areas because they need more watching, more spraying, and more hand labor, but the cash price can be better if the market is right. Stevia I will keep on a small piece too. I finished only primary school, so I do not make it too complicated. I look at what nearby farmers do, what my own field showed last year, and what the seed and fertilizer seller says if it matches what I already know. If I am unsure on fertilizer, I will not cut too hard, because losing yield hurts more than spending a bit extra. For wheat and maize I will stay close to local habit, with enough water at key times. For vegetables I will feed heavier, because if I want head size and fruit setting, I cannot be stingy. I will plough the wheat and maize ground, and for the vegetable plots I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is quicker and easier to manage on this farm size.
